Hi Priya,

Thanks again for the intro last week. BrightLens asked us to confirm how Pinecone + Redwood would handle index availability during sustained outages in their primary vector store (S3 tiering in their architecture). They want a quantifiable resilience story before moving forward with a Q3 pilot.

High level asks from BrightLens:
- Max tolerable read latency during a fallback event (99th percentile)
- Expected token-level cost delta when we route queries to an S3-backed cold index + Redwood fallback model
- Runbook steps for detection, cutover, and re-sync (they want audit logs for each step)
- Commercial question: will Pinecone and Redwood accept a joint SLA write-up for the pilot (30–60 day POC) or do we need a separate procurement addendum?

We can commit our technical side but Pinecone needs to confirm their end-to-end tail latency and consistency story. Mike from Acme Cloud (our S3 partner) is looped for questions about rehydration timelines.

Attached: Pinecone proposed fallback ops (PDF) — baseline SLAs included.

Can we hop on a 30-min call today or tomorrow to align on an ops playbook? BrightLens is hoping to sign off the scope by end of next week.

Best,

Anna — thanks for the clear ask. Quick response and proposed plan from Redwood: 

TL;DR: Redwood can support a deterministic SLO-driven fallback to an S3-backed index with two operational modes — 'graceful-degrade' (serve limited queries with cached KV and approximate nearest neighbours) and 'failover' (route read traffic to a higher-memory model + cold index reads). We will provide:
- A runbook template with detection heuristics, rollback criteria, and audit log events.
- A lightweight telemetry dashboard showing per-route 99/95/50 latency and token-cost delta during the event.
- A short-term SLA addendum for the pilot that maps to BrightLens' acceptance criteria.

Questions for you / Pinecone team:
1) Can Pinecone commit to a documented cold-read tail latency range for the representative BrightLens index sizes (we need 95th/99th for 3x index sizes)?
2) For the commercial language — Redwood is OK with a joint pilot SLA addendum. We do ask that any permanent SLA be negotiated separately in the enterprise contract.
3) On detection: do you prefer a service-health webhook from Pinecone + a Redwood synthetic test as the primary trigger? Or should we have a double-confirm (webhook + synthetic) to avoid flapping?

Proposed immediate next steps:
- Marissa and I will draft the runbook (attaching v0.2).
- Schedule a 30-min alignment today (I’m free 2–4pm PT) or tomorrow morning.
- Pinecone to confirm baseline tail-latency numbers and a contact for DocuSign if we agree on pilot terms.

Anna — copying Marissa and Karthik for technical and contract input.

Thanks,

Putting a technical note in the thread before the call — a few constraints and mitigations we should bake into the runbook:

1) KV cache warm-up: our continuous-batching runtime warms KV caches per-model and per-prefix. During a fallback, we must accept that cold-read latency will be high until a warm-up window. Ops recommendation: serve tail-tolerant queries from a pinned quantized variant for the first 15–30 minutes and gradually route to full-capacity once KV populations reach a threshold.

2) Consistency window: BrightLens uses near-real-time syncs to S3. We need to agree on an eventual-consistency window (we recommend declaring a 2–5 minute window in the runbook). BrightLens should be made aware of possible stale vector embeddings during rehydration.

3) Index version pinning: to avoid drift we must pin a stable index snapshot for the duration of the pilot fallback event; automatic re-merge should be scheduled post-cutover (explicit steps documented).

4) Audit and replay: include steps to capture request/response pairs and to queue replays into a backfill job. That must be an opt-in BrightLens setting for privacy.

I attached a short ops checklist and a sample endpoint policy (ACL snippets) that we'll want Pinecone and BrightLens to sign off on.

If Pinecone can provide 95/99 latency buckets for 50GB/200GB/1TB index sizes, we can include concrete thresholds in the SLA addendum.

Thanks — this is helpful and aligned. Quick answers from Pinecone / Acme: 

- Baseline tail numbers (approx): 50GB -> 95th=180ms / 99th=420ms; 200GB -> 95th=220ms / 99th=550ms; 1TB -> 95th=360ms / 99th=930ms. These are cold-read estimates and depend on S3 regional latency; we can run a benchmark during the pilot to firm them up.
- Rehydration: Acme (Mike) confirms multi-threaded prefetch options; typical initial rehydrate throughput is ~80–120MB/s per worker (region dependent).
- Detection: Pinecone will emit a service-health webhook + metrics stream. We agree a webhook + Redwood synthetic double-confirm is the safest default.
- Commercials: Pinecone can accept a joint pilot SLA addendum. We’ve created a DocuSign envelope for a 30-day pilot NDA & SLA (link below).
